title: Netflix & Cheese
text:
Crafting the perfect cheeseburger is a lot like creating compelling movies or TV shows here at Netflix. It’s all about balance, creativity, and knowing your audience. Just as a great burger needs the right blend of ingredients, unforgettable show or film demands a strong script, layered characters, engaging visuals, and emotional resonance. You can’t rely on one element alone; everything has to come together to deliver an experience that satisfies and sticks with people. And just like how taste trends evolve, audience expectations shift too, resulting in constantly experimenting, refining, and pushing boundaries to serve up something familiar yet fresh every time.
Today, I will be looking at two different sets of data, the Global top 10 and Countries’ Top 10 from the last few years. They will show more insights into the success of our programs here at Netflix. My goal is to find any trends that could allow for future success.
To begin I will look into the Global top 10 data set below.






As you could see, each page represents the Global Top 10 for a different week for one of different 4 programs.

To begin my analysis, I wanted to start with finding out the most succesful Non-English film in the world. It turns out that All Quiet on the Western Front was the most successful one, with it being in the top 10 for 23 weeks.
To stay on the films topic, I went to look which was the longest Film to ever appear on the Global top 10. The result was that Pushpa 2: The Rule (Reloaded Version) was the longest film, with a run time of 224 minutes (Almost 4 hours long).
Next, I want to look into the total global viewership for each of our top program in each category. I computed a data table and got the results below.






It is fair to say that the results are not surprising. All four programs are exceptional, and this is proven by the interaction by customers throughout social media. However, to me, Squid game is the one program that cannot be compared to the rest.

Squid Game is the rare show that turned mass unemployment, existential dread, and childhood nostalgia into a global binge party. What began as a bleak satire on debt and desperation somehow became a worldwide watercooler phenomenon—proof that subtitles don’t scare audiences nearly as much as capitalism does. It has collected over 5 billion views worldwide since its debut. With its candy-colored chaos, moral gut punches, and meme-ready moments, Squid Game didn’t just win ratings—it redefined what a global hit could look like. It showed that you don’t need superheroes or Hollywood budgets to dominate Netflix; you just need a green tracksuit, a catchy song, and the collective realization that we’d all probably lose Red Light, Green Light.
The last thing I wanted to do with the Global top 10 data set was to calculate the total number of views a program had in a certain year. For this exercise, I chose the movie Red Notice and finding their views in 2021. After running some code, I calculated that the movie had a total of 201.7322034 million views in that year.
Next, I moved on to analyze the country top 10’s data set below.






In similarity to the other data table, each page represents an individual country’s Top 10 for a different week for films or tv shows.
To begin my analysis, I first want to figure out how many countries around the globe that Netflix operates in since 2021. The result is 94 countries. However, Netflix does not operate in Russia since the week of 2022-02-27.
Switching back to positive things, I wanted to find the TV show who had the longest run inside the top 10 of any country in the world. Turns out, Pablo Escobar, el patrón del mal had a run of 102 consecutive weeks in the top 10 of Colombia. Having watched the show myself, I could understand its popularity given the context as to what happened in real life back in the 80’s and 90’s.
To keep the positivity going, I stayed with TV shows and analyze which one had debuted in the most amount of top 10’s around the world. After some analysis, I discovered that Emily in Paris - Emily in Paris: Season 2 debuted in the top of 94 different countries. A very impressive tout.
Lastly, I analyze TV shows in the US. I began to search which TV shows had not debuted on the US top 10, but eventually made its way onto it. As you can see below, these are the shows that accomplish that feat. The most recent one to do it was KPop Demon Hunters.






###Press Release 1


Press Release 1

Stranger Things - 5th and Final trip around the sun
Los Gatos, CA — October 2025 — Netflix today announced that the fifth and final season of its global phenomenon Stranger Things will premiere at the end of 2025. As anticipation builds, Netflix reflects on the unparalleled success of the series’ first four seasons, which have left an enduring mark on popular culture and television history.
Across its four seasons, Stranger Things has amassed almost 3 billion total amount of hours in viewrship, placing it among the most-watched series ever on the platform. The series appeared in Netflix’s Global Top 10 for various weeks, with each season sustaining popularity long after its premiere.
The show’s reach extends far beyond its hometown of Hawkins, Indiana: Stranger Things charted in the Top 10 of 93, underscoring its power to connect with audiences across continents. From Brazil to Germany, India to South Korea, the series has proven itself a truly global television event.
When compared with other blockbuster English-language hits, Stranger Things stands in a league of its own. Other shows like Wednesday, The Witcher or even Bridgerton can’t matched the sustained, multinational engagement of Stranger Things.
As the curtain prepares to rise on the final season, fans around the globe can look forward to one last adventure with Eleven, Mike, and the beloved Hawkins crew. The conclusion of Stranger Things is set to be one of the most significant cultural television moments of the decade, cementing its legacy as a defining series of the streaming era.


Press Release 2

Bollywood goes Streaming
Los Gatos, CA — October 2025 Netflix today highlighted the growing popularity of its Hindi-language films and TV shows in India, the world’s most populated country and one of Netflix’s fastest-growing markets.
Over the past few years, Hindi titles on Netflix have been watched for hundreds of millions of hours, with both films and series regularly landing in the Top 10. This strong demand suggests a large and expanding subscriber base in India, as more viewers turn to Netflix for entertainment in their own language.
Recent hits like RRR show how Netflix is connecting with audiences week after week, with Hindi titles appearing in the Top 10 for various weeks. The steady growth reflects not just short-term excitement but long-term loyalty.
By investing in more Hindi originals and expanding its catalog, Netflix is committed to making India a centerpiece of its global strategy.



Press Release 3

The rise of Subtitles
Los Gatos, CA — October 2025— Netflix today announced the rising popularity of non-English language entertainment among U.S. audiences, signaling a major shift in viewing habits and opening new opportunities for international storytelling.
Over the past two years, non-English titles have consistently broken into the U.S. Top 10, from Spanish-language dramas and Korean thrillers to French comedies and Japanese anime. Collectively, these titles have generated hundreds of millions of viewing hours in the U.S., proving that American audiences are increasingly eager to explore stories beyond traditional English-language programming.
Hits such as Squid Game, Money Heist, and Lupin each dominated the U.S. Top 10 for multiple weeks, with Squid Game alone becoming one of Netflix’s most-watched series ever. More recently, non-English films have also surged in popularity, with Hindi, Spanish, and Korean blockbusters drawing strong viewership across the United States.
This trend reflects more than just a cultural curiosity—it highlights a strategic growth opportunity. By expanding investment in dubbing, subtitling, and global marketing, Netflix aims to make international stories even more accessible to American viewers. The company will also continue to partner with creative talent worldwide, ensuring that audiences in the U.S. can experience the diversity of global storytelling.
“Non-English language titles are no longer niche—they are becoming mainstream in the U.S.,” said a Netflix spokesperson. “As we look ahead, we’re excited to bring even more international stories to American homes, strengthening our commitment to entertainment that transcends borders.”

title: Affordability for 500
text:
How can something truly be called a necessity if so many people can’t afford it?
In a perfect world, one could live wherever they wanted. Spoiler alert, this world is far from perfect.
Affordability isn’t just about price—it’s about access, opportunity, and fairness in everyday life.
But then again, you have NIMBY’s who think their opinions matter more than others.









NIMBY’s are our biggest opposition going back years. Unfortunately for them, many of us, like myself, are here to evicerate them. With your help, we will be able to turn those N’s into Y’s and start the YIMBY epidemic.
In the following page, I will show findings about housing affordability in NYC. In addittion, we will dive into what a federal YIMBY-incentive program could look like. At the end, I will introduce an new bill that will change the landscape of affordable housing for future generations.
First, we are going to familiarize ourselves with the data will be using. Below, you will see the relationships between all of our data tables and how they can be related to one another.









Next, we will see some of the findings that we can extract from this data. To begin, we seek out the top 5 CBSAs that permitted the largest number of new housing in the 2010’s.






As we can see, the CBSA that permitted the largest number of new housing units between 2010 and 2019 was CBSA in Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land, TX Metro Area.
Next, we’ll take a look a CBSA 10740, located in Alburquerque, New Mexico and analyze their yearly addition of new housing units.









As shown in the graph above, the number of new housing units permitted were on a steady decline up until the COVID pandemic. Then, in 2021, CBSA 10740 had its highest number of new housing units permitted, with 4021 units.
Next, we go over to look at average income per state, more specifically in the year 2015.









The map above shows all 50 states average income. However, it does not include additional US territories that are also included in the data. Therefore, more analysis has to be completed. That’s when you figure out that the District of Columbia had the highest average individual income for 2015, coming in at $33,233. Something, people in the government should be familiar too.
Next findings show which CBSA had the most amount of data scientists in the last 5 years.






In 4 out of the last 5 years, San Francisco has had the most data scientists. To get a better understanding of these part of the data, I wanted to see the NYC CBSA and if they have ever had the most data scientists. After taking a closer look at more previous years, you are able to find that 2015 was the last year that the NYC CBSA led the country for data scientists.
The last thing we take a look at initially, is the total wages in the NYC CBSA. We look specifically into the wages that come from the finance and insurance industries to figure the percentage this is of the total wages.









We look at various years to find no trend. However, we are able to find the peak in the year 2014, with about 5% share of the total wages for the CBSA for the year.
To keep on the trend of familiriaty with the dataset, we will see more visualizations to show different types of relationships.









The visualization above shows us the relationship between monthly rent and average household income per CBSA in 2009.
Each dot in the scatter plot refers to a different CBSA.
As you could see, there is a positive correlation between the cost of rent and household income.









The next visualization shows the relationship between total employment and total employment in the health care and social services sector across different the 5 CBSAs with the highest employment total.
Over time, depending on the CBSA, the share is volatile and can either decrease or increase. The time where it mostly increases is in the year 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.









The third visualization is the evolution of the average household size over time.
We highlighted two specific CBSAs, the NY and LA ones, to take a closer look at the evolution.
We can infer that the average household size, especially in those CBAs, has been steadily decreasing.
The next two visualizations will have to deal with rent burden.
We are going to create an rent-to-income ratio and compare the results around the CBSAs.









In the visualization above, we take a look at the rent burden in the CBSAs (33100 + 33124) in the Miami metro area. To understand better, the dashed red line represents the 30% affordability benchmark.
As you could see, the rent burden for South Floridians has been on an exponential rise post pandemic.









The next visualization shows the rent burden in 2023 for CBSA’s across the nation.
We are highlighting the CBSAs with the highest and lowest rent burdens.
To stay with the trend from the first rent-burden visual, one can assume that the rent burden in the entire state of Florida is increasing in all areas of the region.
Next, we are going to look at housing growth within the CBSAs.
We are going to construct two metrics; one will allow us to see the housing growth based on population of a CBSA and number of new housing units permitted for the year. The other metric will compare the housing permits to the population growth over a 5 year lookback windown.
Lets first take a look at the first metric.










After coming up with our metric, we are able to separate the top 10 and bottom 10 CBSA’s in terms of instantaneous housing growth.
To explain in English terms, lets take a look at the first table.
Myrtle Beach CBSA was one of the most construction-intensive metros in the entire country in 2023 — building new housing far faster than typical cities its size. (Over nine standard deviations above the national average)
In contrast in the second table, we can see see that the Decatur CBSA built noticeably fewer new homes per resident than most U.S. metro areas — about one standard deviation below average.
Next, we will take a look at the second metric.










After coming up with our second metric, we are able to separate the top 10 and bottom 10 CBSA’s in terms of rate-based housing growth.
To explain better, we can see that in 2023, the Springfield CBSA had a housing_growth_rate_std of +2.1026, meaning it was building housing at a rate significantly higher than most U.S. metro areas relative to its recent population growth.
Now on the other side of the spectrum, in 2023, the Manhattan CBSA had a housing_growth_rate_std of −0.141, meaning it was very close to the national average, with just a slight tendency to underbuild relative to population growth.
The last metric we will take a look is a composite score that combines the first two metrics.
Once we figured out the metric, we are going to identify the CBSA’s that do well and poor with this measure. This will give us an idea to the Metro areas that are most YIMBY friendly.










Therefore, in 2023, the Punta Gorda CBSA had a housing_growth_composite_std of +3.5413, meaning its overall pace of housing development was exceptionally strong.
That makes Punta Gorda one of the most construction-active metros in the country when you consider both its raw building rate and how well housing supply is keeping up with population growth.
On the other hand, in 2023, the Morgantown CBSA had a housing_growth_composite_std of −1.137, meaning its overall housing growth pace was moderately below the national average.
A value of −1.14 indicates Morgantown’s combined housing indicators — both how much it’s building and how well it’s keeping up with population growth — were a little over one standard deviation below what’s typical across U.S. metros.
The last thing we’ll do before we introduce the bill is to visualize the relationship between our Rent Burden and Housing Growth metrics.









In the scatter plot above, we are trying to interpret if there is any correlation between average rent burden and average housing growth while also trying to show the size of population of each CBSA.
Each dot in the scatter plot represents a different CBSA.
Unfortunately, we do not see any correlation between the two.









In the line graph above, we spotlight the CBSA in New York (35620) to show the similarities between the trend of both their rent burden and housing growth from 2014 to 2018.
As you can see, you may be able to see that trend for both metrics follow similar paths. However, it is not clear to show that they both follow the same trends.
The last visualization we are going to see is to search which CBSAs identify as the most YIMBY.
To determine, we have 4 criteria that each has to meet: - had relatively high rent burden in the early part of the study period - have had a decrease in rent burden over the study period - have had population growth over the study period - have had above-average housing growth during the study period









From the visual above, we get the list below of CBSAs that meet all 4 criteria. In total, it is 27 CBSAs that are most YIMBY.


 [1] "Punta Gorda"                "Lakeland-Winter Haven"     
 [3] "Salisbury"                  "Burlington"                
 [5] "Ocala"                      "Auburn-Opelika"

Now that we have studied the data extensively, it is time to have a call to action.
It is my honor to introduce the bill below.
The “Rebuild the American Dream Act”

title: The “Rebuild the American Dream Act”
text:
The Challenge
Across the country, families are spending more on rent than ever before. In many metropolitan areas, housing supply has failed to keep up with population growth. This shortage drives up rents, limits household mobility, and increases the cost of living for working families. At the same time, the lack of new housing construction strains local labor markets, especially in essential sectors such as education and health care.


The Proposal
The Rebuild the American Dream Ac Act would create a federal incentive program that rewards local governments for adopting pro-housing reforms. The goal is to protect renters and align infrastructure investment with growth. Cities that make it easier to build homes near jobs and transit would be eligible for competitive federal grants that help finance infrastructure, workforce housing, and mixed-income development.


Sponsorship
To ensure bipartisan appeal and geographic balance, this bill has two leading sponsors. The primary sponsor is the representative from Cleveland, Ohio. The co-sponsor of the bill is the representative from Manhattan, NY. With the help from them, we have representation from both NIMBY and YIMBY metro areas.


Additional Support
A successful housing reform coalition requires people with direct economic stakes in affordable housing. Two especially relevant groups are health-care professionals and teachers. Both face challenges finding housing near their workplaces. By encouraging new development, this bill would reduce commute times, improve retention, and expand disposable income—benefiting not only these workers but also the broader local economy.


Metrics
Our approach uses two intuitive, transparent indicators to guide funding and accountability:
Rent Burden: The share of a typical household’s income spent on rent, standardized around a 30% benchmark. A value near zero indicates an average burden, while positive values signal affordability stress.
Housing Growth: A composite of two measures—new housing permits relative to total population, and permits relative to five-year population growth. This captures both current construction intensity and whether cities are building fast enough to keep pace with demand.


Importance
Cities that build homes relieve pressure on rents, support workforce stability, and improve local competitiveness. For high-rent areas, federal support can help overcome regulatory inertia and spur equitable growth. By linking funding to measurable outcomes, this bill ensures accountability and rewards communities that act to make housing affordable again.


Conclusion
The Rebuild the American Dream Act offers a pragmatic, bipartisan solution to the housing crisis. It combines data-driven metrics, local flexibility, and tangible incentives for reform—empowering both fast-growing and housing-constrained cities to deliver the homes American families need.

title: NYC Tree Party
text:
New York City’s trees are one of our greatest public assets. They shade our streets, clean our air, and make our neighborhoods more livable — yet not every community benefits equally from this natural infrastructure. As a City Council member, I believe it’s time we address this imbalance by dedicating additional funding to expand and maintain our urban forest, particularly in districts that have been historically overlooked.
The NYC Department of Parks and Recreation (DPR) manages nearly 900,000 trees citywide, covering over 30,000 acres of public parkland. This is a tremendous achievement, but the data shows that some council districts have denser, healthier tree populations than others. To better understand these disparities, I am analyzing the NYC TreeMap dataset to examine how trees are distributed across districts, which species dominate, and how factors like tree health and diversity vary throughout the city.
By grounding this proposal in data, my goal is to build a strong case for targeted investment — a program that not only plants more trees in under-served areas but also ensures long-term care and maintenance. Expanding the city’s tree canopy isn’t just about beautification; it’s about equity, public health, and resilience. Every New Yorker deserves to walk down a shaded block, breathe cleaner air, and share in the environmental and social benefits our trees provide.
First, let’s take a look at the data and look at all the city council districts by borough.









As you could see, there are 51 city council districts in New York City.
Once we have visualized all the districts, next we are going to visualize the trees that within each one.
